title: What is a REST API?
overview: A REST API is an interface that allows applications to communicate using HTTP requests. It follows REST principles to exchange data between client and server.

example.title: REST API Flow
example.content:
Client
 ↓
HTTP Request
 ↓
REST API Server
 ↓
Response

title: HTTP Methods in REST API
overview: REST APIs use HTTP methods to perform different operations on resources.

example.title: HTTP Methods
example.content:
GET → Read data
POST → Create data
PUT → Update data
DELETE → Remove data

title: Creating GET API
overview: GET APIs are used to retrieve data from the server.

title: Creating POST API
overview: POST APIs are used to send new data from the client to the server.

title: Updating and Deleting Data
overview: PUT and DELETE methods are used to modify and remove existing resources from the server.

example.title: Update and Delete
example.content:
PUT → Update existing user
DELETE → Remove user

title: Working with JSON Data
overview: REST APIs commonly exchange data in JSON format because it is lightweight and easy for applications to understand.

title: API Testing
overview: API testing verifies whether endpoints work correctly by checking requests, responses, and returned data.

title: Topic Summary
overview: You learned REST API concepts, HTTP methods, creating endpoints, handling JSON data, and testing APIs.

example.title: Quick Revision
example.content:
✔ REST APIs connect client and server.
✔ HTTP methods perform operations.
✔ JSON transfers data.
✔ APIs should be tested properly.
